summary: This follow-up refines the eight inherited weight-two targets without redeclaring them. Lobachevsky analysis and Kummer reduction give a finite rational Fourier algorithm with a uniform certified error, including inputs on the unit circle. Milnor supplies the ideal-tetrahedron angle formula using the metric and volume owned by GeometricTopology. A matrix-unit calculation detects an error in the published Dynkin normalization proof; the map-level comparison to the Burgos-normalized Borel regulator remains explicitly open. P.2 owns the analytic comparison and ideal-tetrahedron identity; K3BlochGroups and ArithmeticQuantumTopology consume them.

nodes.title: Lobachevsky function
nodes.statement: For every real theta define Lambda(theta)=-integral from 0 to theta of log|2 sin t| dt, using the signed native interval integral and Real.log. The integrand is locally integrable despite its logarithmic singularities. The normalization is Milnor’s Lambda; the Clausen function Cl_2(2theta) is 2 Lambda(theta), not Lambda(theta).
proofSteps: Use intervalIntegrable_log_sin and log|2 sin t|=log 2+log(sin t) away from sin t=0; the exceptional multiples of pi have measure zero.
Define the signed interval integral. Its additivity and substitution t↦-t give oddness; pi-periodicity follows from sin(t+pi)=-sin t and integral_log_sin_zero_pi.
Local integrability gives continuity of the primitive; away from sin theta=0 the continuous-integrand fundamental theorem gives derivative -log|2 sin theta|.

sources.match: The precise integral normalization and elementary symmetries.

acceptance: The pi/4 test distinguishes Lambda from twice Lambda.
No positivity assertion is made for all angles: Lambda(2pi/3)=-Lambda(pi/3).

uses.how: Its sum at the three dihedral angles is the tetrahedron volume.
Its angle values identify the existing Bloch–Wigner function.

nodes.title: Lobachevsky Fourier series
nodes.statement: For every theta in R, the absolutely convergent series (1/2) sum_{n>=1} sin(2n theta)/n^2 has sum Lambda(theta); convergence is uniform in theta.
proofSteps: For 0<r<1 expand -log(1-r exp(2it)) using P.1/classical-polylogarithm at weight one, and integrate its real part on a compact interval.
Let r increase to 1. For t away from pi Z use the log-sine identity; near each zero use an integrable logarithmic bound. Native intervalIntegrable_log_sin supplies the limiting integral.
The integrated coefficients are bounded by 1/(2n^2). Real.summable_nat_pow_inv with p=2 yields absolute and uniform convergence, permitting the endpoint passage. Both sides vanish at theta=0.

sources.match: The series is twice Lambda; its uniformity follows from the p-series majorant.

acceptance: The n=1 coefficient is sin(2theta)/2.
At theta=pi/4 this gives half the alternating odd reciprocal-square series.

nodes.title: Lobachevsky duplication identity
nodes.statement: For every real theta, Lambda(2theta)=2 Lambda(theta)+2 Lambda(theta+pi/2).
proofSteps: Use lobachevsky-fourier and absolute convergence to add the two series termwise.
sin(2n(theta+pi/2))=(-1)^n sin(2n theta); odd n cancel. Reindex the even terms n=2k to obtain the factor 2.

sources.locator: Appendix, Lemma 1, distribution identity with n=2
sources.match: The n=2 specialization used to evaluate the half-space sector integral.

acceptance: Theta=pi/6 is consistent with Lambda(2pi/3)=-Lambda(pi/3).

nodes.title: Bloch–Wigner Fourier series on the circle
nodes.statement: For w in C with norm w=1, sum_{n>=1} Im(w^n)/n^2 is absolutely convergent and has sum D(w), including w=1. Here D is exactly the P.1 Bloch–Wigner function, extended by D(0)=D(1)=0.
proofSteps: For r<1 use the P.1 Li_2 power series at rw. Bound its coefficients by 1/n^2 independently of r.
Pass to r=1 using P.1 closed-disc continuity and the summable p-series majorant; take imaginary parts.
Since log norm w=0, the Bloch–Wigner correction vanishes. At w=1 every imaginary coefficient and D(1) are zero.

sources.locator: I.3, p.11, series immediately after equation (2)
sources.match: The circle series, including endpoints by continuity.

acceptance: w=i gives the alternating odd reciprocal-square series.
w=-1 gives zero; conjugating w negates the series.

nodes.title: Uniform unit-circle Fourier error
nodes.statement: For w in C with norm w=1 and integer N>=1, |D(w)-sum_{n=1}^N Im(w^n)/n^2|<=1/N. The bound is uniform, including w=1 and points arbitrarily close to it.
proofSteps: Use unit-circle-fourier to express the difference as the absolutely convergent tail.
Bound |Im(w^n)| by norm(w^n)=1. Apply the native sum_Ioc_inv_sq_le_sub with k=N and let the upper endpoint tend to infinity.
This gives sum_{n>N} 1/n^2<=1/N; no separation from 1 or the real axis is needed.

sources.match: The stated explicit tail is a proved consequence using the pinned p-series bound, not a quoted source bound.

acceptance: N starts at 1; no division-by-zero bound at N=0.
The bound applies to the exact rational unit shapes.

nodes.title: Kummer unit-circle reduction
nodes.statement: For z in C minus {0,1}, put u0=z, u1=1/(1-z), u2=1-1/z and wj=uj/conj(uj). Then each wj has norm 1 and D(z)=(D(w0)+D(w1)+D(w2))/2. The identity holds in both half-planes and on the real axis; no argument branch or cut exclusion is added.
proofSteps: All uj are nonzero for the stated z. Multiplicativity of the native complex norm proves that every wj lies on the unit circle.

Prove Kummer’s identity using P.1/bloch-wigner-differential: differentiate the difference on the upper and lower half-planes, substituting the three rational functions and the logarithm identities for their absolute values.

The derivative of the difference is zero on each half-plane. Its limit at a real point z not equal to 0 or 1 is zero by P.1/single-valued-continuity and the real-axis vanishing of D. Extend to all remaining real points by those same facts.
With wj=exp(2i arg uj), the unit-circle and Lobachevsky Fourier formulas give the global angle expression. Its upper-half-plane specialization agrees with the inherited P.2/lobachevsky-identity.

sources.match: Precisely the three conjugate ratios; division by 2 is essential.

acceptance: z=i has w0=-1 and w1=w2=i; the formula reads D(i)=(0+2D(i))/2.
A real z not equal to 0 or 1 gives wj=1 and both sides zero.

nodes.title: Rational unit-circle shapes
nodes.statement: For a rational pair z=(a,b), produce rational pairs W_j(z), j=0,1,2. For z=0 or 1 set all W_j=(1,0). Otherwise set rho(x,y)=((x^2-y^2)/(x^2+y^2),2xy/(x^2+y^2)), W0=rho(a,b), W1=rho(1-a,b), W2=rho(a-1,b) multiplied by the conjugate of W0, using (x,y)(s,t)=(xs-yt,xt+ys). This is a computable rational construction; its complex interpretation is established in rational-unit-shapes-correct.
proofSteps: Check the two exceptional rational pairs by decidable equality and use the stated total extension.
On valid input, a^2+b^2 and (a-1)^2+b^2 are nonzero. The displayed rational formulas are therefore the exact conjugate ratios, not approximations.
Use native Complex.mul_re and mul_im for compatibility; the rational-square calculation gives x_j^2+y_j^2=1.

sources.match: The displayed rho arithmetic is the explicit rational specialization of the source ratios.

acceptance: All divisions take place in Q; no real-to-rational approximation is invoked.

uses.how: Replaces the three complex ratios by exact rational coordinates.
Provides inputs of norm one with rational powers.

nodes.title: Exact complex interpretation of rational shapes
nodes.statement: If (a,b) is neither (0,0) nor (1,0), let z=a+bi in native C. Embedding W_j into C gives respectively z/conj z, (1/(1-z))/conj(1/(1-z)), and (1-1/z)/conj(1-1/z), and all three embedded pairs have norm one.
proofSteps: Establish nonzero denominators from the rational input hypotheses.
For W0 and W1 use complex coordinate division; for W2 multiply the ratio of z-1 by the conjugate of the ratio of z.
Apply native coordinate multiplication and norm_def; the identities are rational polynomial calculations after clearing the nonzero denominators.

sources.match: This comparison promotes the construction’s compatibility API used in the error theorem.

acceptance: The second shape has plus 2(1-a)b in its imaginary coordinate; the opposite sign gives the wrong D(i) test.

nodes.title: Finite rational Fourier sum
nodes.statement: For w=(x,y) in Q^2 and N in N define q0=(1,0), q_{n+1}=(q_n.re*x-q_n.im*y,q_n.re*y+q_n.im*x), and S_N(w)=sum_{n=1}^N q_n.im/n^2 in Q. The recurrence is finite and uses exact rational arithmetic. No unit-norm hypothesis is required to define S_N; it is required for the uniform analytical error.
proofSteps: Use a primitive recursion on n for the pair coordinates and a finite sum over indices 1 through N.
Induction using native Complex.mul_re and mul_im identifies q_n with the coordinates of (x+iy)^n.
Conjugation negates imaginary coordinates, so S_N(conj w)=-S_N(w); the zero-length sum is zero.

sources.match: Finite exact sums of the same coefficients, with a rational coordinate recurrence.

acceptance: The recurrence computes powers, rather than repeating the first imaginary coordinate.

uses.how: Evaluates the three circle sums with a prescribed finite length.
The compatibility theorem converts the rational answer to a native real Fourier sum.

nodes.title: Rational and native Fourier sums
nodes.statement: For every rational pair w=(x,y) and N in N, the coercion of S_N(w) to R equals sum_{n=1}^N Im((x+iy)^n)/n^2, with powers and imaginary projection in Mathlib C.
proofSteps: Prove the coordinate-recursion identity by induction; multiplication uses exactly the pinned mul_re and mul_im formulas.
Coercion Q→R preserves finite sums and quotients. Every denominator n^2 for 1<=n<=N is nonzero.
No norm restriction is used; the lemma separates algebraic correctness from the unit-circle analytic tail bound.

sources.match: Promotes the rational finite-sum compatibility API needed by the error proof.

acceptance: N=3 and w=i give 1-1/9, with the n=2 term zero.

nodes.title: Certified rational Bloch–Wigner approximation
nodes.statement: For every rational pair z and precision p in N define A(z,p)=(1/2) sum_{j=0}^2 S_{3*2^p}(W_j(z)). This is a total computable function Q^2×N→Q; the exceptional pairs 0 and 1 give zero. It is the explicit implementation proposed for the inherited P.2/certified-numerics contract, whose generic function is not redeclared here.
proofSteps: Compute the three rational unit shapes, choose the positive integer N=3*2^p, and evaluate the three exact finite rational sums.
Combine them with coefficient 1/2. The construction has no choice of a rational close to an unknown real.
The error is supplied by rational-fourier-error. Runtime and bit sizes are not asserted polynomial in p: this deliberately simple uniform algorithm uses exponentially many terms.

sources.locator: I.3, equation (2) and following Fourier series
sources.match: Combines the source formulas with the proven uniform tail to specify an effective algorithm.

acceptance: The coefficient 1/2 and the length N=3*2^p are fixed, not parameters hidden in an existence assertion.
At p=1 and z=i the answer exceeds 2^-1, giving a valid positive certificate.

uses.how: Instantiates the inherited rational approximation and error contract.
Rational enclosures certify values of finite sums of admissible Gaussian-rational generators.

nodes.title: Rational Fourier error certificate
nodes.statement: For a valid Gaussian-rational input z=a+bi and p in N, |(A((a,b),p):R)-D(z)|<=1/(2*2^p)<=2^-p. Hence A(z,p)>2^-p certifies D(z)>0, A(z,p)<-2^-p certifies D(z)<0, and |A(z,p)|>2^-p certifies D(z)!=0. For any finite integer combination sum n_i[z_i], the rational sum sum n_i A(z_i,p_i) has error at most sum |n_i|2^-p_i. This does not assert that an arbitrary combination lies in B(F); the algebraic boundary certificate stays V.6’s.
proofSteps: Use rational-unit-shapes-correct to embed all three computed shapes as the Kummer ratios of norm one.
Apply Kummer reduction and rational-fourier-compatibility to rewrite D(z) and A(z,p) in the same three components.
Apply unit-circle-fourier-tail at N=3*2^p to each component. The triangle inequality gives 3/(2N)=1/(2*2^p), hence the inherited precision bound.

Derive the strict sign and nonvanishing implications by interval containment. For a finite integer combination, apply the triangle inequality with integer absolute values; never infer nonvanishing merely from a nonzero decimal.

sources.match: Error certification is a mathematical consequence of these identities and the pinned tail estimate, not a source claim of a fast algorithm.

acceptance: At z=i,p=1, 209/225-1/2>0 proves a strictly positive lower bound.
No |z|<1 assumption appears; the valid unit-circle input i is covered.
A comparison of two outputs is decisive only when their difference exceeds the sum of the error radii.

nodes.title: Milnor’s ideal-tetrahedron angle formula
nodes.statement: Let T be a nondegenerate ideal geodesic tetrahedron in the explicit curvature -1 hyperbolic 3-space metric imported from GeometricTopology. For its three dihedral angles at any one vertex alpha,beta,gamma (opposite edges have equal angles), alpha,beta,gamma>0 and alpha+beta+gamma=pi. Its unoriented Riemannian volume is finite and equals Lambda(alpha)+Lambda(beta)+Lambda(gamma). Ordered volume is its orientation sign times this value. Under r(infinity,0,1,z)=z, Im z>0 is positive and these angles are arg z, arg(1/(1-z)), arg(1-1/z). Combined with the inherited lobachevsky-identity, this proves the inherited hyperbolic-volume target.
proofSteps: Import the explicit hyperbolic metric, model isometries and Riemannian volume from GeometricTopology layers 7–8. The early Part II ideal-boundary, measurable region and orientation interface remains a precise supplier gap.

Move one ideal vertex to infinity and make the opposite face the unit hemisphere in the upper-half-space model. The metric is (dx^2+dy^2+dh^2)/h^2 and volume density h^-3 dx dy dh; apply the supplied change-of-model compatibility, rather than defining a new unrelated volume.

Project to the triangle inscribed in the unit circle and split an acute triangle into six right sectors. For a sector with angle a in (0,pi/2), integrate h from sqrt(1-x^2-y^2) to infinity, y from 0 to x tan a, x from 0 to cos a. The height integration supplies the essential factor 1/2.

After the elementary y integral and x=cos t substitution, the sector equals [-Lambda(pi/2+a)+Lambda(2a)+Lambda(pi/2-a)-Lambda(0)]/4. Oddness, periodicity and lobachevsky-duplication simplify it to Lambda(a)/2.

Sum the six sectors. For an obtuse inscribed triangle use the signed decomposition about its circumcentre: the difference of sector indicators equals the triangle indicator almost everywhere. Absolute integrability justifies subtraction; the same sector formula gives the sum for every positive alpha,beta,gamma summing to pi.

Transport back by the imported orientation-preserving model isometry. Reflecting complex coordinates reverses ordered volume. Invoke the inherited P.2/lobachevsky-identity for the Bloch–Wigner identification; QT.5 consumes this result and supplies manifold triangulations and Bloch invariants.

sources.locator: Appendix, Lemma 2 and complete proof, pp.18–20
sources.match: The independently calibrated half-space integral proves the volume normalization.
The complex shape/angle interpretation and orientation convention.

Provides a second distributional route; its c3 derivation is not imported as a proved calibration. Independent review also found the factor-six error in the preceding Theorem 7.1 (source issue E24); Milnor supplies the volume scale.

acceptance: The regular ideal tetrahedron has volume 3 Lambda(pi/3)=D(exp(i pi/3))>0.
A reflected ordered tetrahedron has the negative volume.
A real shape other than 0 and 1 is flat and has ordered volume zero; it is outside the nondegenerate angle hypotheses.

nodes.title: Corrected weight-two matrix-unit calibration
nodes.statement: Use the unnormalized Alt_3 of the published Goncharov paper: for E2=e12 wedge e21 wedge e22 in gl_2(C), Alt_3 Tr(e12 e21 e22)=-3 and C2(E2)=-3/2 when C2=(1/2)Alt_3 Tr as in equation (66). The Burgos trace polynomial Phi3=-(1/6)Alt_3 Tr of BorelRegulators:R.4 therefore evaluates to +1/2 on the same ordered matrices. These are explicit cochain evaluations, not an asserted equality of continuous, measurable or K-theory regulator classes.
proofSteps: Read the source’s Alt definition, equation (66), equation (67) and the displayed evaluation on published p.39 together; see source issue Polylogarithms/E22.
Expand all six permutations using eij ekl=delta_jk eil. The three even terms have trace zero; the three odd terms have trace one. Thus the alternating trace is -3.
Multiply by 1/2 for the printed C2 convention and by -1/6 for the independently owned R.4 Phi3 convention.

The printed Theorem 5.7 yields a formal coefficient 1/12 at n=2 and Corollary 5.10 prints 1/24 against b2, but the proof calibration fails this test. Re-derive the class coefficient, beta_DR comparison, Tate division and the natural Suslin/Hurewicz map before concluding the inherited borel-comparison’s exact scalar. This is the recorded normalization gap, not a hidden prerequisite supplied by R.7.

sources.match: The literal elementary-matrix test is corrected by an exact six-permutation calculation; source issue E22.

acceptance: Reversing e12 and e21 changes the sign to +3/2, which still does not give the printed 1.
Do not use this calculation alone to assign a Borel-to-D scalar.

requests.need: Import the explicit curvature -1 hyperbolic metric and its native Riemannian volume density, with upper-half-space chart density h^-3 and change-of-chart compatibility. Existing upstream work is not replanned.

Import the three-dimensional hyperbolic model and its orientation-preserving model isometries. General JSJ, Mostow and manifold volume minimization are not proof prerequisites for an ideal tetrahedron.

Degree-three comparison for GL_2(C) and stabilized GL_N(C): differentiable/continuous cochains, invariant forms, relative Lie cohomology and van Est with explicit coefficient and orientation conventions. Add a compatible measurable-cocycle comparison for the P.2 D(cross-ratio) representative, including repeated configurations. The latter is an extension request rather than a claim that the current AF.1a text supplies it.

gaps.title: Map-level Borel normalization, including the failed source calibration
gaps.detail: The inherited up-to-Q× comparison is retained, with P.2 as its analytic owner. Goncharov Theorem 5.7’s printed n=2 class coefficient 1/12 and Corollary 5.10’s 1/24 are not accepted as an audited exact endpoint because the displayed C2(E2)=1 conflicts with equations (66)–(67): it equals -3/2. Re-derive the coefficient from the boundary/symmetric-space integral; compare beta_DR and AF.1a van Est, the R(1) generator 2pi i and the real-coordinate division, the r(infinity,0,1,z)=z sign, and the natural V.4 Suslin map after rationalization. R.4/trace-cocycle supplies the independently normalized Burgos class. Export the exact scalar to the existing R.7/weight-two-bloch-wigner consumer; do not import that consumer as a premise.

sourceIssues.reason: Of the six products in Alt_3 Tr(e12 e21 e22), the three even-permutation traces are 0 and all three odd-permutation traces are 1. sourceIssues.reason: Use the projective unit-ball (Klein) model from the source, with y0=0 and yi=epsilon e_i, i=1,2,3. Choose lifts (yi,1) and boundary lift (x,1), x in S^2. Then mu_yi/mu_y0=(1−epsilon x_i)^−2. With outward boundary orientation the integral is 8 epsilon^3 integral_{S^2} x1 dx2 wedge dx3 + O(epsilon^4) = (32pi/3) epsilon^3 + O(epsilon^4). The geodesic simplex is the Euclidean coordinate tetrahedron; the normalized volume density tends to 1, so its volume is epsilon^3/6 + o(epsilon^3). Their ratio tends to 64pi, contradicting the printed 32pi/3. Lemma 7.3 computes the leading exterior-form coefficient but transferring it to simplex volume needs the factor 3!.
